# Cache avalanche results

These are local observations from repeatedly reading 1,000 independently cached keys while their expiry times follow different schedules. They show load shape in one controlled model, not universal production capacity.

## Environment

- Date: 2026-09-02
- Host: Apple M4, 10 logical CPUs
- OS: macOS 26.5.1, Darwin arm64
- Go: 1.26.6
- Command: `go run .`
- Repeats: 3 runs per case

## Experiment Variables

- Keys: 1,000
- Base TTL: 100 ms
- Expiry spread window: 500 ms
- Read interval and origin-attempt bucket: 10 ms
- Origin latency: 20 ms
- Origin capacity: unlimited and 50 concurrent loads

## Results

| Expiry schedule | Origin capacity | Origin calls | Max attempts/bucket | Attempt span | Peak active | Peak queued | P99 queue wait |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| aligned | unlimited | 1000.0 | 1000.0 | 1.122ms | 1000.0 | 0.0 | 0s |
| jittered | unlimited | 1000.0 | 31.0 | 497.204ms | 69.3 | 0.0 | 0s |
| staggered | unlimited | 1000.0 | 23.7 | 499.556ms | 62.7 | 0.0 | 0s |
| aligned | 50 | 1000.0 | 1000.0 | 1.128ms | 50.0 | 950.0 | 391.43ms |
| jittered | 50 | 1000.0 | 30.0 | 496.624ms | 50.0 | 17.0 | 4.441ms |
| staggered | 50 | 1000.0 | 23.7 | 500.9ms | 50.0 | 13.0 | 1.87ms |

Values with decimals are averages across the three runs.

## Observations

Every schedule made 1,000 origin calls. Jitter and staggering did not remove any refresh work.

Aligned expiry placed all 1,000 origin attempts into one 10 ms bucket. With unlimited capacity, all 1,000 loads overlapped. With capacity 50, 950 loaders queued at the peak and P99 admission wait reached about 391 ms, close to the time required to process 1,000 fixed 20 ms loads in batches of 50.

Random jitter spread attempts over about 497 ms. Its busiest 10 ms bucket averaged 30 attempts, reducing unlimited peak active loads from 1,000 to about 69. With capacity 50, random clustering still briefly created a queue, but P99 queue wait fell to about 4.4 ms.

Deliberate staggering spread attempts across about 500 ms and produced a smaller busiest bucket than random jitter in this run. Under capacity 50, it still briefly reached the limit because 20 ms loads overlap multiple 10 ms request ticks, but P99 queue wait was about 1.9 ms.

## Caveats

- Scheduler timing makes bucket counts and spans vary slightly between runs, which is why the result records averages.
- The read loop touches every key every 10 ms. This intentionally ensures prompt refresh; real key popularity is usually skewed.
- The capacity semaphore models only admission. It does not model database connection setup, query contention, adaptive latency, queue rejection, or request deadlines.
- Origin latency remains fixed under overload. Real downstream latency often increases as concurrency rises, making aligned expiry worse than this model.
- Random jitter uses deterministic seeds so runs are reproducible. Different seeds change local clusters but not the underlying tradeoff.
